text: IN THE COURT OF THE JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE FIRST CLASS, Pune. Criminal Complaint No. 4125/2021. Rekha Bose (Complainant) versus Subrata Ghosh (Accused). The accused issued cheque No. 493369 dated 2 June 2021 for ₹6,90,000 towards repayment of a hand loan. The cheque was returned unpaid on 30 August 2021 with the remark "funds insufficient". Despite a legal notice dated 3 December 2021, the accused failed to pay within 15 days. The accused is convicted under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, sentenced to simple imprisonment for 9 months and directed to pay compensation of ₹13,80,000 to the complainant under Section 357(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure within 62 days.

IN THE COURT OF THE ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, Indore. Criminal Appeal No. 294/2023. The appellant Anil Deshmukh challenges the judgment dated 12 November 2023 convicting him under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act for dishonour of a cheque of ₹87.5 lakh. The appellant has deposited ₹17,50,000, being 20% of the cheque amount, under Section 148 of the Act. The statutory notice was served on 25 October 2022, but the complaint was filed only on 17 March 2023, beyond the one month allowed by Section 142, so the complaint was time-barred. The appeal is allowed, the conviction is set aside and the deposit of ₹17,50,000 shall be refunded to the appellant within 34 days.

IN THE COURT OF THE SESSIONS JUDGE, Varanasi. Bail Application No. 2779/2023. HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT Madras. Criminal Miscellaneous Application No. 3237 of 2020. IN THE COURT OF THE CIVIL JUDGE (SENIOR DIVISION), Howrah. Original Suit No. 435 of 2019. STATE INFORMATION COMMISSION, Howrah. Second Appeal No. 7426/2020. The appellant Shobha Gaikwad filed an RTI application on 9 March 2020 seeking copies of land mutation records. BEFORE THE MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, Coimbatore. MACP No. 2078 of 2020. The claimants are the widow and 2 minor children of Subrata Ghosh, aged 44, who died on 20 May 2020 when his motorcycle was hit by a truck bearing registration No. MH-12-AB-7692 driven rashly. The deceased earned ₹16,500 per month. Adding 40% or 25% for future prospects according to age, deducting one-fourth for personal expenses and applying a multiplier of 14, the Tribunal awards total compensation of ₹26.69 lakh with interest at 8% per annum from the date of the petition, 25 December 2020. The insurer shall deposit the amount within 48 days.

BEFORE THE MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, Indore. MACP No. 1236 of 2020. The Tribunal assesses permanent disability at 16% and awards ₹7,49,000 in total, including ₹3,09,500 towards medical expenses and ₹89,500 for pain and suffering, with interest at 8% per annum. The insurer shall deposit the award within 43 days of the order dated 26 May 2020.
